correctness.rationale: The degree-two endpoint neighbor-parity condition forces all four vertices of the first two rungs to have distinct colors. At an interior degree-three vertex, two already distinct neighbor colors prohibit a third repetition (the only legal positive degree-three multiplicities are 1+1+1 or 3), forcing pairwise distinct neighbors and propagating four distinct colors at each successive pair of rungs. Thus exactly the distance-two constraints of L_n^2 hold. For four distinct previous colors, a new rung E,F has (k-3)^2 candidate pairs minus k-4 equal pairs, a constant k^2-7k+13 factor. k<4 vanishes because of the initial K4, while at k=4 each extension is forced and 24 initial assignments persist. Independent direct predicate enumeration and transfer cases corroborate, not replace, the induction.

value.rationale: Strong odd coloring generally permits three equal colors around a degree-three vertex, so equality with square-coloring sets is a nontrivial rigidity property even for this clawed natural family. The exact labeled-palette polynomial, stable chromatic number, and unique four-coloring orbit provide complete meaningful combinatorial information.

final_claim: For every open two-row ladder L_n with n>=2, proper strong-odd colorings are exactly proper square-graph colorings; their k-labeled-palette count is k(k-1)(k-2)(k-3)(k^2-7k+13)^(n-2), yielding chi_so=4 and 24 four-palette colorings.
